title: Positive-dimensional locally algebraic closed subsets have infinitely many closed points
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $Z\subseteq X$ is an irreducible closed subset [def-weil-irreducible-components] with positive topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then $Z$ contains infinitely many closed points of $X$ [def-weil-closed-points].

source.place: Tags 0478 and 0A21, together with the affine positive-dimension argument in Commutative Algebra (a positive-dimensional finitely generated domain has infinitely many maximal ideals)

proof.text: The locally finite type structure morphism makes X a Jacobson space by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] (Mathlib: LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace). Its closed subspace Z is Jacobson by JacobsonSpace.of_isClosedEmbedding applied to the subtype inclusion.

Suppose Z intersect closedPoints X [def-weil-closed-points] is finite. Pull back along the injective subtype inclusion Z -> X. For this closed embedding, IsClosedEmbedding.preimage_closedPoints identifies the pullback with closedPoints Z, so Z has finitely many closed points. Mathlib JacobsonSpace.discreteTopology then gives the discrete topology on Z.

source.place: Tag 0478, Jacobson-space consequence; Mathlib.Topology.JacobsonSpace, IsClosedEmbedding.preimage_closedPoints and JacobsonSpace.discreteTopology

proof.text: A discrete space has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most zero (Mathlib topologicalKrullDim_zero_of_discreteTopology), because each nonempty irreducible subset is a singleton. This contradicts the assumed positive dimension of Z. Thus Z intersect closedPoints X is infinite. Irreducibility is not required in this stronger topological argument, but its hypothesis in the declaration is kept unchanged.
